+*This model was contributed to Hugging Face Transformers on 2026-11-16.*
+Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the [Swiss AI Initiative](https://huggingface.co/swiss-ai) that accepts
+text, images, and audio and generates text. It extends the [Apertus](./apertus) language model with the
+for audio. The EMU3.5 vision tokenizer is an image-only VQGAN with the same encoder as [Chameleon](./chameleon)'s,
+unlike the [Emu3](./emu3) tokenizer, which adds temporal layers for video. It assigns codes by the largest inner
+product with the codebook instead of the smallest L2 distance.
+The media tokenizers convert images and audio into discrete tokens, which the language backbone processes
+alongside text in a shared input vocabulary. The output vocabulary contains only text tokens. The integration
+includes the media encoders and quantizers; it does not support image or audio generation, or training the
+Use the processor's chat template to prepare a conversation with images and audio. It loads the referenced
+media, resamples audio, and constructs the model inputs automatically.

+- **Tokenizer precision:** Both media tokenizers require `float32` for stable code assignments.
+  `from_pretrained` preserves this precision when loading the language backbone in half precision. Avoid
+  casting the entire model to a lower precision or running the tokenizers under mixed-precision autocast.
+  If quantizing the model, ensure the backend excludes both media tokenizers.
+- **Output vocabulary:** Returned logits cover only `text_config.output_vocab_size` when set, otherwise
+  `text_config.vocab_size`. Input-only multimodal tokens cannot be generated. Mask these tokens with `-100`
+  in training labels, and restrict generation constraints to tokens within the output vocabulary.

+[WavTokenizer](https://huggingface.co/papers/2408.16532) encodes 24 kHz mono audio into discrete tokens using a
+single codebook, at 40 or 75 tokens per second depending on the checkpoint. It can also reconstruct audio
+This implementation supports inference with [`WavTokenizerModel`] for encoding and decoding, or
+[`WavTokenizerEncoderModel`] for encoding only. The 40-token-per-second variant supplies the audio tokenizer
+for [Apertus 1.5](./apertus1p5). Training the codec is not supported.
+This model was contributed by the [Swiss AI Initiative](https://huggingface.co/swiss-ai).
+These checkpoints are ready to load with `from_pretrained`:
+Load a speech clip, resample it to the checkpoint's sampling rate, and encode and reconstruct it:
+- **Audio inputs:** The feature extractor expects mono audio at its configured sampling rate; it does not
+  resample or downmix. The example uses `load_audio` to handle both. Decoding can add trailing samples due to
+  internal padding, so the example trims the reconstruction to the original length.
+- **Batching:** Padding clips of different lengths can change their codes. Encode clips separately when
+  you need the same codes as processing each clip on its own.
+- **Precision:** Load and run the tokenizer in `float32` (the default). Lower precision can change code

+"""Assemble Apertus 1.5 from a text backbone, original EMU3.5 vision weights, and converted WavTokenizer.
+Sources accept local directories or Hub `repo_id[@revision]`; use FP32 media-tokenizer checkpoints.
+Conversion validates source formats, precision, and vision weight keys/shapes. Optional `--verify` loads
+the full output model and checks loading, precision, token mappings, generation, and multimodal forwards.
+Verify an existing composite without conversion or source downloads:
+Use `--processor_only` with text/audio sources to update processor assets without rewriting weights.
+Be aware that this script does not perform the lm-head pruning. It must be done before.
